title: Appointed members named as directors or officers of organizations their body’s department funds
question: Which members of boards, commissions and advisory committees are named as a director or officer of an organization that holds a contract with the department the body sits in?
finding: 8 member-and-organization pairs with a rare name; 0 are confirmed by the member’s own Form 700, which names the organization. The departments paid these organizations $13.7 million in the years of the notices. Of 13 people who have filed a Form 700 as members of the SoMa Community Stabilization Fund advisory committee (the panel in the United Playaz case), 7 share a name with a director or officer on a notice for that office’s grants or on a funded organization’s return in the same years. 1 pair with common names: counted, not listed.
how: The same notices, matched to Form 700 filers whose filing is for a board, commission, committee or authority and who are not on that department’s payroll. A pair is kept when the notice’s department is the one the member’s body belongs to (the Mayor’s Office of Housing and Community Development is read from the position line) and the notice falls within a year of a filing year.
limits: Advisory bodies are often built from people who run local organizations; the seat is disclosed and the rule is recusal on the organization’s own item, which only minutes can show. The department, not the panel, signs the grant, and many of the grants listed come from programmes the panel does not advise on. Rows not confirmed by the member’s own Form 700 are name matches.
